query: Research on refractory multicomponent alloys has emphasized exceptional strength at room and elevated temperatures, while mechanical assessment has relied mainly on compression and has included relatively few tensile studies. WFeNiMo fragments released more chemical energy than tungsten-alloy fragments in thin-steel-target penetration tests, and HfZrTiTa0.53 was reported at 786 MPa yield strength, 1314 MPa compressive strength, and 13.5% terminal strain. This evidence establishes strength and energetic promise but leaves limited tensile ductility, load-bearing reliability, and processability unresolved. Subject to preserving strength and impact-triggered energy release, what single testable hypothesis identifies an intervention for HfZrTiTa0.53 that could improve tensile ductility and uniform elongation? Include the intervention, causal mechanism, directional or quantitative outcomes relative to the reported baseline, the applicable temperature, loading mode, and strain-rate limits, prior evidence from the cited studies, and matched compression, tension, and impact tests with a result that would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: Applying deep cryogenic treatment (DCT) after laser additive manufacturing of HfZrTiTa0.53 will improve its tensile ductility and uniform elongation while maintaining its strength and impact-triggered energy release.
generation.material_initial_state: HfZrTiTa0.53 produced by conventional processing (e.g., laser melting deposition) that exhibits high compressive strengths (786 MPa yield, 1314 MPa maximum) but limited tensile ductility (~13.5% terminal strain in compression-based indicators and few tensile data points).
generation.intervention: Expose as-deposited HfZrTiTa0.53 samples to deep cryogenic treatment by immersing them in liquid nitrogen (≈ -196 °C) for a soaking duration between 24 and 48 hours.
generation.conditions: Room temperature mechanical testing under quasi-static loading (strain rate approximately 10^(-3) s^(-1)); matched tests include tensile, compression, and impact assessments.
generation.structural_mediator: Induced lattice distortion and potential phase transition (e.g., formation of nanoscopic twin boundaries or slip system activation) that enhance plasticity.
generation.mechanism: The DCT is expected to increase internal residual stresses uniformly and promote beneficial microstructural modifications (e.g., twin formation, symmetry breaking) that yield additional active slip systems; this increases uniform elongation under tensile loading while preserving high strength and impact energy release capabilities.
generation.predicted_outcome: Compared to untreated samples, DCT-treated HfZrTiTa0.53 will show at least a 15% improvement in uniform tensile elongation (e.g., from ~13.5% toward 15.5%+ elongation) while retaining yield strengths within 10% of baseline values and matching impact-triggered energy release levels.
generation.baseline: HfZrTiTa0.53 as produced by LMD exhibits compressive yield strength of 786 MPa, compressive strength of 1314 MPa, and about 13.5% terminal strain (with tensile ductility data being limited).
generation.boundary: The hypothesis is applicable for room temperature, low strain-rate tensile tests; its validity under elevated temperatures or high strain rates is not assumed.
generation.uncertainty: It is uncertain whether the beneficial effects observed in a similar Hf-Nb-Ta-Ti-Zr BCC high-entropy alloy after DCT (as reported for Hf0.25NbTa0.25TiZr) will translate quantitatively to the non-equiatomic HfZrTiTa0.53 alloy.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two groups of HfZrTiTa0.53 samples formed via laser melting deposition. Subject one group to deep cryogenic treatment in liquid nitrogen for 24–48 hours and leave the other group untreated. Perform standardized tensile tests at room temperature under a strain rate of ≈10^(-3) s^(-1) alongside compression tests and impact-triggered penetration tests to assess energy release.
measurements: Uniform tensile elongation and tensile yield/ultimate strengths
Impact energy release (e.g., chemical energy measured in penetration tests)
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the DCT-treated samples do not exhibit a statistically significant improvement (≥15% increase) in uniform tensile elongation relative to untreated samples while keeping their yield strengths within 10% of the baseline and showing comparable impact-triggered energy release, the hypothesis is falsified.

## Abstract
AbstractHfNbTaTiZr high-entropy alloy has wide application prospects as a biomedical material, and the use of laser additive manufacturing can solve the forming problems faced by the alloy. In view of the characteristics of the one-time forming of additive manufacturing methods, it is necessary to develop non-mechanical processing modification methods. In this paper, deep cryogenic treatment (DCT) is first applied to the modification of a HEA with BCC structure, then the post-processing method of DCT is combined with laser melting deposition (LMD) technology to successfully realize the coordinated improvement of forming and strength–ductility synergistic improvement in lightweight Hf0.25NbTa0.25TiZr alloy. The final tensile strength of the alloy after DCT treatment is 25% higher than that of the as-cast alloy and 11% higher than that of the as-deposited alloy, and the elongation is increased by 48% and 10%, respectively. In addition, DCT also achieves induced phase transition without additional deformation.Keywords: laser melting deposition, high entropy alloy, deep cryogenic treatment, 3D printing, defects, strength–ductility synergistic improvement
## 1. Introduction

HfNbTaTiZr high-entropy alloy can be improved by increasing the lattice distortion of the alloy []. The above characteristics mean more modification methods can be applied to Hf-Nb-Ta-Ti-Zr alloys.
At present, the casting forming of HEAs is facing some problems due to their high melt viscosity, and laser additive manufacturing (AM) technology can effectively solve this problem [,,]. Laser melting deposition (LMD) technology has high energy density and complex-shape-forming ability, which can solve the problem of HEA forming and accumulate thermal stress in as-deposited alloy samples [].
